claims.statement: KNF Recommendation S requires banks to perform comprehensive quantitative and qualitative creditworthiness assessment using verified information and says irregular or unstable income does not preclude lending when an individualized assessment supports regular repayment.

Polish law expressly includes preparatory document handling within mortgage intermediation and requires intermediaries and agents to transmit the information needed for the creditor's assessment; the creditor, not the proposed tool, remains responsible for the formal creditworthiness decision.

Bank documentation and income-history requirements for business owners are materially more complex than standard employment and can vary by tax form, timing, and bank policy; ING lists multiple business-specific document branches, while PKO notes bank-specific models and commonly varying activity-history requirements.

Direct incumbents already automate broad mortgage comparison and preparation: FinPack claims use by 70% of Polish mortgage experts, calculations across 20 banks, common-form generation, and bank integration, while Lendi reports 3,000 experts and one application workflow for multiple banks.

KNF reported 797 mortgage intermediaries and 6,884 registered agents at year-end 2024, and an official notice reported 967.5M PLN of total mortgage-intermediation revenue in 2023; this demonstrates a real channel but not its software budget or willingness to switch.

An AI system intended to evaluate a natural person's creditworthiness is listed as high-risk under the EU AI Act, and the CJEU has held that an automated repayment-probability value can fall within GDPR automated-decision rules when a third party relies strongly on it; therefore applicant scoring is a materially different and more regulated product than document and policy support.

No public tariff for the incumbent broker systems was located in the reviewed pages, so a 300 to 600 PLN monthly seat price and network implementation fee are validation hypotheses rather than evidenced market prices.

contrary_evidence: FinPack already claims very broad expert penetration and offers bank comparison, affordability calculations, common-form generation, bank integrations, and BIK or BIG access, directly overlapping the proposed core workflow.
Lendi combines thousands of experts, document lists, multi-bank applications, and consumer distribution, making a greenfield broker-network entry structurally difficult.

Banks retain their own documented assessment procedures and can change internal policies; historical broker outcomes may become stale and may encode discrimination rather than stable causal lender rules.

If the product evaluates applicant creditworthiness rather than only documents and policy eligibility, AI Act high-risk obligations and GDPR automated-decision exposure materially increase cost and liability.
The official channel size and revenue do not establish per-seat software willingness to pay, and no public incumbent price was found.

economics.acquisition_route: Recruit one mid-sized licensed broker network for a paid JDG-file-completeness pilot using synthetic or properly deidentified historical files, measure rework and preparation time, then expand by advisor teams; no network or accounting partner commitment is evidenced.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Scenario, not forecast: 1,200 active seats at 450 PLN monthly produce 6.48M PLN ARR. At 35% EBITDA, 3.5x EBITDA, and 65% founder ownership, founder equity is about 5.16M PLN in years 7 to 10, before liabilities and without double-counting retained earnings. The target equals roughly 17% of the 6,884 agents reported for 2024 and is therefore demanding given entrenched incumbents; failure to validate a differentiated network channel invalidates the path.
economics.founder_time: 15 to 20 hours weekly for a narrow rules-and-document product, outcome monitoring, and one enterprise pilot; the broker owns applicants and licensed activities.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Target 70% to 85% after document-processing costs, policy operations, security, compliance review, customer support, and network-specific configuration; bank integrations would reduce early margins.
economics.payback: Unknown until time logs show the frequency and cost of JDG exceptions. A buyer case requires measured reduction in document chase, policy lookup, or avoidable resubmission, not a claimed increase in approvals.
economics.pricing: Validation hypothesis, not observed competitor pricing: 300 to 600 PLN per active advisor monthly, or 50,000 to 120,000 PLN annual network license plus scoped implementation; avoid per-approval pricing that encourages misleading success claims.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Use recurs per complex file and policy changes create ongoing value, but incumbent suites, policy freshness, and low case frequency can weaken retention.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A versioned, provenance-tagged map of lender policy, document requirements, manual overrides, and lawfully aggregated outcomes for defined irregular-income archetypes
fingerprint.customer: Polish mortgage-broker networks and specialist teams serving applicants with JDG, B2B transitions, seasonal income, multiple income sources, or nonstandard tax forms
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: One mid-sized broker-network pilot, then network and accounting-platform partnerships that already aggregate JDG applicants
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Reviewable document extraction, versioned deterministic policy rules, missing-evidence gate, scenario provenance, and aggregate policy-performance reporting sold as B2B SaaS
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: A broker network pays a recurring advisor-seat or team license plus a bounded implementation fee
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A broker receives an irregular-income mortgage file and must determine the missing documents, applicable lender-policy rules, and defensible human submission order

founder_fit: Strong fit with the founder's Polish context, finance interest, quantitative modeling, document extraction, and preference for systemized B2B distribution rather than a public persona.

A deterministic, synthetic-data prototype and one network pilot can fit 15 to 20 founder hours weekly; licensed intermediaries must own consumer conversations and a specialist must review financial-services, AI Act, GDPR, and fairness boundaries.
The 75,000 PLN initial budget permits a narrow non-production pilot and security work, but not speculative bank integrations or a high-risk credit-scoring compliance program.
risks: A model or interface may be interpreted as a guaranteed approval prediction, consumer recommendation, or creditworthiness score despite disclaimers.
Tax returns, bank statements, household expenses, liabilities, and application outcomes are high-impact personal financial data requiring strong security and governance.
Historical outcomes can reproduce discriminatory patterns or lender-specific selection effects and become stale after policy changes.
FinPack, Lendi, or a broker network can add a specialist JDG rule layer using their installed base and bank relationships.
Obtaining reliable, versioned policy inputs may require bank or network cooperation that is not publicly evidenced.
A part-time founder may be unable to support frequent policy operations, enterprise procurement, and sensitive-data incident response without a committed channel partner.

structure.control_point: The licensed broker's documented file-completeness and lender-policy review immediately before a human chooses a submission route
structure.critical_dependency: A broker network must supply timely policy knowledge and lawfully governed outcome feedback while the product remains outside bank credit decisions, automated applicant scoring, and consumer advice

thesis: Create broker-side document and policy support for Polish mortgage files involving sole-proprietor and other irregular income. The product would parse submitted documents into a reviewable checklist, apply versioned deterministic lender-policy rules, show missing evidence and calculation provenance, and let a licensed intermediary choose what to present and where to submit. Outcome data should initially be retained only as lawfully governed, coarse policy-performance aggregates. The product must not approve credit, produce a consumer credit score, guarantee acceptance, or replace the bank's statutory creditworthiness assessment.
title: JDG Mortgage Exception Engine for Polish Broker Networks
uncertainties: Complex irregular-income cases per advisor per month, baseline rework time, and which edge cases FinPack or Lendi still handle poorly.
Whether any broker network will permit a paid side-by-side pilot or provide policy updates and deidentified outcome labels.
Lawful controller or processor roles, purpose limitation, retention, and aggregation standard for pooled application outcomes.
Whether lender-fit ranking would be treated in practice as creditworthiness evaluation, regulated advice, or ordinary intermediary preparation.
Incumbent contract pricing, network switching cost, bank-integration access, and feasible gross retention for a new vendor.
Measured willingness to pay for a JDG-only overlay when broad incumbent platforms are already deeply distributed.
